newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials push higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials push higher in active trade.

text.p: Strength in a number of heavy-weight stocks pushed the Zimbabwean industrial index higher on Wednesday in active trade, but dealers said shares were likely to remain trapped in a narrow range due to a hesitant mood.
They said that investors were holding back, awaiting new issues to join the market to mop up the excess liquidity around.
"Industrials closed up with heavies like Barclays behind it. Sentiment appears to be less bullish than it was two or three weeks ago, but it's not bearish," one dealer said.

"Players are holding off slightly in order to receive the new issues that are lining up. Shares are likely to hold around the current, narrow trading range until the new issues absorb the excess liquidity that's around," he added.
The 57-counter industrial index put on 45.71 points to 10,226.53 points, pushed up by a 100 cent gain in both Barclays and Porthold to 3,300 and 1,900 cents respectively.
Gains were also recorded in Tanganda which added 25 cents to 475, and ZSR which rose 25 cents to 450 cents.
But losses were seen in IHL which cut 50 cents to 1,550, Alloys which lost 50 cents to 700, and FMB which closed 100 cents weaker at 6,400 cents.
Dealers said that volumes had been fairly large, indicating that the market was content with its current levels.
"Quite a bit of volume went through. This means that we have found levels in the market that we are happy with, for the time being," one trader said.
Traders said that the promise of new issues was offering alternatives for investment and had removed the market's earlier urgency to chase up shares.
Trans Zambezi Ltd (TZI) announced earlier on Wednesday that its share purchase offer had closed on Tuesday over-subscribed. The company plans to list on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange in mid-February.

The seven-share mining index shed 41.28 points to end the day at 968.59 points. Falgold lost five cents to 90 and Rio Tinto shed 400 cents to 2,000. Wankie, Ashanti, Bindura and Alloys Mines were untraded.
